The twelve brochures

As built in the game: each in a style of its own, with photographs taken in the game and the game's own prices and steps. Sold from three street racks (the park gate, Market St, the Hudson walk) at $2. READ one from your pack, click the cover to open it, and GO THERE takes you to the place. A full set pays $50.

The lettering uses each computer's own typefaces, so the headings look a little different on a Mac, a PC and a phone.

1 · PIRATE WRECK! a glossy rack card · goes to FISHING & SCUBA

Dive the
PIRATEWRECK!
SHARKS · SUNKEN GOLD · GEMS 55 METRES UNDER THE HUDSON

No. 1 · THE MARKET

REAL SUNKEN TREASURE

  • A 48 m pirate ship, broken in two, her black flag still on the mast.
  • Swim INSIDE: the stern cabin and a hold full of barrels.
  • SEVEN chests of old coins and gems, full again every day.
  • FOUR sharks on guard. They bite!
  • Raise the ship's bell with a SALVAGE WINCH: it pays $150.
THINGS TO DO IN THE MARKET

ANYONE CAN DIVE

  1. Buy a SCUBA SET at FISHING & SCUBA and WEAR it from your pack. The tank holds 5 minutes of air and fills again, free, whenever you are out of the water.
  2. Add GOGGLES and a HEADLIGHT. It is dark down there.
  3. Step off the quay. Hold SPACE to go down, SHIFT to come up.
  4. About 25 seconds down: the ship. Double-click a chest.
THINGS TO DO IN THE MARKET

WHERE

FISHING & SCUBA, on the Hudson row. The wreck lies on the deepest bed of the Hudson, 55 m down.

2 · THE FISH ARE BITING. the Fisherman's own photocopy · goes to FISHING & SCUBA

FISHING & SCUBA · THE HUDSON ROW
THE FISHAREBITING.
17 kinds. The Hudson and the lake. I buy what you land.
ask me aboutthe old catfish
No. 2 · THE MARKET

What's in the water

Eleven kinds in the Hudson: white perch, tomcod, eel, blue crab, catfish, shad, flounder, bluefish, striped bass, and the Atlantic sturgeon, 40 kg of him.

Six more in the park lake, up to the northern pike. Day, dusk and night each bring different fish.

Now and then the hook brings up a boot, a tin can, a message in a bottle or a sunken chest.

THE OLD CATFISH lies under the pier between 2 and 4 in the morning. Cut bait. Once a day.

THINGS TO DO IN THE MARKET

How you do it

  1. Hold your rod.
  2. By the water press F.
  3. Hold SPACE for power, let go to cast. B changes bait.
  4. The float dips: SPACE, and quick.
  5. Hold SPACE to reel. Ease off when it says EASE. Pull A or D against a run.
  6. Take it off the hook. X or ESC when you are done.

Crab pot: press P facing the water. Come back for the buoy.

THINGS TO DO IN THE MARKET

WHERE

The long pier at the foot of the way through to the Hudson. Tackle at FISHING & SCUBA. Rowboats at the foot of the pier.

WHAT IT COSTS

FISHING ROD$15
WORMS, CUT BAIT$1
CRAB POT$25
CARBON ROD$60
SURF ROD$180
COOLERS$20 to $120
ROWBOAT, A TRIP$5

WHO'S WAITING

HOW TO ADOPT

  1. Go into a shop. Double-click a cage, or THE ADOPTION BOOK.

  4. ESC, then PETS: feed it, take it out, choose where it rides. Head, shoulder, flying or walking.
  5. Press E to pet it.

A fed, loyal pet finds you dollars.

4 · Birds & Butterflies a park-service folder · goes to CENTRAL PARK

Central Park
Birds &Butterflies
25 butterflies · 13 birds · a journal to fill
No. 4 · THE MARKET

What to look for

Twenty-five butterflies fly the park, twelve common and thirteen rare, from the Monarch to the Apollo and the Homerus Swallowtail. A rare one is worth $40 to $250.

Thirteen birds, from the house sparrow to the red-tailed hawk. A first sighting pays: $40 for the oriole, $60 for the scarlet tanager, $80 for the hawk.

The WILDLIFE page of your journal: crow, great horned owl, mallard, honeybee, bumblebee. A full page pays $50.

THINGS TO DO IN THE MARKET

In the field

  1. Hold the BUTTERFLY NET and double-click a butterfly. You carry 5; jars hold 20, 50 or 100.
  2. IDENTIFY it in your pack, then sell it or RELEASE it.
  3. Double-click a bird: WATCH, TAME with birdseed, or CATCH with a bird net and a cage.
  4. Scatter seed or hang a FEEDER, and stand still.
  5. Hold BINOCULARS, click to raise them. The wheel focuses.
  6. Double-click a creature and keep still 5 seconds to log it.
THINGS TO DO IN THE MARKET

WHERE

All of Central Park. THE BUTTERFLY STALL and THE BIRD STALL stand on the park wall, west of the gate.

5 · EAT ONE AND FLY a 1970s poster · goes to THE MUSHROOM STALL

The Mushroom Stall
EAT ONEAND FLY
Fourteen power mushrooms. Eighteen wild ones.
No. 5 · THE MARKET

What they do

  • FLIGHT: five minutes in the air, up through the clouds, cape on.
  • SHRINK: two-fifths your size. GROW: twice your size.
  • JUMP: two and a half times as high.
  • BREATH: 20 more seconds under water.
  • And NIGHT VISION, INVISIBILITY, STRENGTH, SPEED, KEEN EYE, HEALING, CURE POISON, LUCK and FIREPROOF.

Wild in the park: 18 kinds, MEADOW BUTTON to LION'S MANE. Ink cap and black trumpet after rain, oyster at dawn, GHOST CAP by night, deep in the park. RED CAP, FLY AGARIC and MOONGLOW are poison.

THINGS TO DO IN THE MARKET

How to fly

  1. Buy a FLIGHT MUSHROOM at THE MUSHROOM STALL.
  2. Eat it from your pack.
  3. Press G to take off.
  4. W A S D to fly. SPACE up, SHIFT down.
  5. Press G to land.

To pick a wild one, double-click it on a park lawn.

THINGS TO DO IN THE MARKET

WHERE

THE MUSHROOM STALL, on the park wall east of the gate. Wild ones grow on the lawns of Central Park.

6 · PARK HONEY a honey-jar label · goes to THE BEEKEEPER'S STALL

The Beekeeper's Stall
PARKHONEY
Keep bees. Six honeys. One only by moonlight.
No. 6 · THE MARKET

Six honeys

The flowers within eight tiles of the hive decide the honey: wildflower, clover, sunflower, lavender or rose.

MOON HONEY is made only at night, deep in the park, and is worth ten times wildflower.

A frame fills every half hour, up to four times faster among flowers. Ten frames to a hive, three hives to a keeper.

THINGS TO DO IN THE MARKET

Keeping bees

  1. Buy a BEEHIVE, a SMOKER, a VEIL and EMPTY JARS.
  2. Stand on a park lawn where flowers grow thick. In your pack press SET IT HERE.
  3. Leave it. The hive fills in real time.
  4. Come back. The smoker quiets the bees; the veil keeps stings off.
  5. Double-click the hive and TAKE HONEY.
  6. LIFT IT to move the hive.
THINGS TO DO IN THE MARKET

WHERE

THE BEEKEEPER'S STALL, on the park wall west of the gate. The Village Gardener keeps it and buys your honey and wax.

WHAT IT COSTS

A BEEHIVE$40
BEE SMOKER$12
BEEKEEPER'S VEIL$15
EMPTY HONEY JAR$1

7 · The Art Museum a museum leaflet · goes to THE ART MUSEUM

Market St
The ArtMuseum
53 paintings. Admission free.
No. 7 · THE MARKET

The collection

Fifty-three paintings hang three to a wall around an atrium that rises to a skylight. A glass elevator serves every floor.

The Night Watch. The Milkmaid. The Great Wave. Washington Crossing the Delaware. Madame X.

Double-click any painting to see it full screen, at the full resolution of the museum that owns it.

THINGS TO DO IN THE MARKET

Your visit

  1. Walk in. Admission is free.
  2. THE INFORMATION DESK shows the floor plan.
  3. Double-click a painting to look closely.
  4. Take A GUIDED TOUR WITH ROSIE around the first floor.
  5. Double-click THE ELEVATOR BUTTONS for the other floors.

The sealed vault

Three dials and a star chart, new each night. The clues are on the cornerstone, on the founder's statue, in a note at the bookstore and on the sky poster by the door.

THINGS TO DO IN THE MARKET

WHERE

THE ART MUSEUM, at the east end of Market St.

WHAT IT COSTS

11 · THE SKY TONIGHT an observatory programme · goes to YOUR APARTMENT

From your own window
THE SKYTONIGHT
A telescope and a microscope in every apartment
No. 11 · THE MARKET

Through the telescope

The real sky over New York, tonight: the stars of the Yale Bright Star Catalogue, the planets, the Moon, the ISS passing over, this year's comets, the meteor showers at their real rates.

Today's Sun from NASA's Solar Dynamics Observatory, sunspots and all.

Real clouds too. If New York is overcast, so is your eyepiece.

THINGS TO DO IN THE MARKET

How to observe

  1. Go home. Double-click the TELESCOPE.
  2. Choose an eyepiece and focus.
  3. GO TO finds a target. The clock drive keeps it in view.
  4. Fit the solar filter before you look at the Sun.

Under the microscope

Pond water alive with microbes. Make slides from what you carry: stones in polarised light, wings, spores, pollen, feathers. Objectives from 4x to 100x.

THINGS TO DO IN THE MARKET

WHERE

YOUR APARTMENT. Both instruments are already there.

WHAT IT COSTS
